<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par64" />{{GHGmargin-letter|64|h}}
3. The following are a few rarer anomalies; in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=יִֽצֲחַק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=6}} (elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=תִּצְחַק}}, &c., in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=יִצְחָק}}, cf. {{GHGpar|10|g}} (c) and {{GHGpar|63|n}}); {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֵחַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=5}} (for {{GHGheb|text=וָאֶֽאֱחַר}}); in the {{GHGterm|perfect Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶֽחֱרוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=28}} (perhaps primarily for {{GHGheb|text=אִֽחֲרוּ}}; according to {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=אֵֽחֲרוּ}} would be expected), and similarly {{GHGheb|text=יֶחֱֽמַ֫תְנִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=51|verse=7}} for {{GHGheb|text=יִחֲֽמַ֫תְנִי}}; in the {{GHGterm|imperative Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=קָרַב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=37|verse=17}} (cf. above, {{GHGpar|52|n}}); finally, in the {{GHGterm|imperative Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הַרְחַק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=21}} and {{GHGheb|text=הַמְעַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=69|verse=24}}, in both cases probably influenced by the closing consonant, and by the preference for ''Pathaḥ'' in {{GHGterm|pause}} (according to {{GHGpar|29|q}}); without the pause {{GHGheb|text=הַרְחֵק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=4|verse=24}}, &c.; but also {{GHGheb|text=הַנְחַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=4|verse=11}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|64|i}}
4. As {{GHGterm|infinitive Hithpaʿēl}} with a suffix we find {{GHGheb|text=הִתְיַחְשָׂם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=8|verse=1}}, &c., with a firmly closed syllable, also the {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=מִתְיַחְשִׂים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=7|verse=64}}; Baer, however, reads in all these cases, on good authority, {{GHGheb|text=הִתְיַֽחֲשָׂם}} &c.—The quite meaningless {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=ונאשאר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=9|verse=8}} (for which the {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} requires the equally unintelligible {{GHGheb|text=וְנֵֽשֲׁאַר}}) evidently combines two different readings, viz. {{GHGheb|text=וְנִשְׁאָר}} (''part. Niph.'') and {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֶשָּׁאֵר}} (''imperf. consec.''); cf. König, {{GHGcite|title=Lehrgebäude}}, i. p. 266 f.—In {{GHGheb|text=יְתָֽאֳרֵ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=13}} (also {{GHGheb|text=יְתָֽאֲרֵ֫הוּ}} in the same verse) an {{GHGterm|imperfect Pôʿēl}} appears to be intended by the Masora with an irregular shortening of the ''ô'' for {{GHGheb|text=יְתֹֽאֲר׳}}; cf. {{GHGpar|55|b}} {{GHGheb|text=מְלָשְׁנִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=101|verse=5}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}; on the other hand Qimḥi, with whom Delitzsch agrees, explains the form as {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, with an irregular {{GHGheb|text=־ֳ}} for {{GHGheb|text=־ֲ}}, as in the reading {{GHGheb|text=אֲלַקֳּטָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=2.7}}; cf. {{GHGpar|10|h}}.

5. A few examples in which {{GHGheb|text=א}}, as middle radical, entirely loses its consonantal value and quiesces in a vowel, will be found in {{GHGpar|73|g}}.
<section end="par64" />
<section begin="par65" />{{GHGpar-heading|65|Verbs Third Guttural, ''e.g.'' {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלַח}} to send||<ref>Verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} in which the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} is ''consonantal'' obviously belong also to this class, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גָּבַהּ|translate=to be high}}, {{GHGheb|text=תָּמַהּ|translate=to be astonished}}, {{GHGheb|text=מָהַהּ}} (only in ''Hithpalpel'') ''to delay''.</ref>}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|65|a}}
'''1.''' According to {{GHGpar|22|d}}, when the last syllable has a vowel incompatible with the guttural (i.e. ''not'' an ''a''-sound), two possibilities present themselves, viz. either the regular vowel ''remains'', and the guttural then takes ''furtive Pathaḥ'', or {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} (in pause {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}}) takes its place. More particularly it is to be remarked that—

(''a'') The unchangeable vowels {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=וֹ}}, {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} ({{GHGpar|25|b}}) are always retained, even under such circumstances; hence ''inf. abs. Qal'' {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלוֹחַ}}, ''part. pass.'' {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלוּחַ}}, ''Hiph.'' {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁלִיחַ}}, ''imperf.'' {{GHGheb|text=יַשְׁלִיחַ}}, ''part.'' {{GHGheb|text=מַשְׁלִיחַ}}. So also the less firm ''ō'' in the ''inf. constr.'' {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלֹח}} is almost always retained: cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלַח}}, in close connexion with a substantive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=58|verse=9}}, and {{GHGheb|text=גְּוַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=20|verse=3}}. Examples of the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} with suffixes are {{GHGheb|text=בְּבָרְחֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=35|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּפִגְעוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=35|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=לְרִבְעָהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=18|verse=23}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|65|b}}
(''b'') The {{GHGterm|imperfect}} and {{GHGterm|imperative Qal}} almost always have ''ă'' in the second syllable, sometimes, no doubt, due simply to the influence of the guttural (for a tone-long ''ō'', originally ''ŭ''), but sometimes as being the original vowel, thus {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁלַח}}, {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלַח}}, &c.; with suffixes {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁלָחֵ֫נִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלָחֵ֫נִי}}, see {{GHGpar|60|c}}.<section end="par65" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
